label: Copy phase, weak preference for outputting g or v
explanation: Diffuse candidate-high unit (~1% of steps). 95% of activation mass falls in the copy phase (rate 2.2%), and almost none comes from original-phase steps; it rarely fires on the first occurrence of a token. Within the copy phase it is most common at recall_idx 1-4 and when the token being output is g (14.6x lift) or v (11x), less so when the next output is v or s. The strongest activations come at copy steps that output g, often in g-g or g-v runs (e.g. input a/DEL -> output g). Even so, only about 13-15% of copy steps that output g/v fire, so no simple token- or position-based predicate gets good precision. Best dev F1 was ~0.20 (precision 0.13, recall 0.43, mass recall 0.50). Not explained.
